**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 31, verses 7–10:**

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[7–10] ﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly, as though he did not hear them, as though there were deafness in his ears. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Bliss,﴾ [Luqman: 8] ﴿abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ [Luqman: 9] ﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you can see, and He placed firm mountains upon the earth lest it shake with you, and He dispersed therein every kind of moving creature. And We sent down water from the sky and caused to grow therein every noble kind of plant.﴾ [Luqman: 10]

﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he turns away﴾, i.e., he turns away from them. ﴿arrogantly, as though he did not hear them, as though there were deafness in his ears﴾, i.e., a heaviness preventing hearing. ﴿So give him tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Bliss﴾ [Luqman: 8] ﴿abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ [Luqman: 9] ﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you can see﴾ [Luqman: 10]. The pronoun refers to the heavens, and it is a proof by their seeing them as unsupported, in reference to His saying ﴿without pillars﴾ [Luqman: 10], just as you say to your companion: "I am without a sword or a spear, you see me." The clause has no grammatical position (la mahalla lahu), either because it is resumptive (mustanafah), or it is in the genitive position (mahall al-jarr) as a qualifier of "pillars," or it means "without visible pillars"; that is, He supported it with a pillar that cannot be seen, which is its being held up by His power. Thus it is in al-Kashshaf (by al-Zamakhshari). ﴿And He placed firm mountains upon the earth﴾ [Luqman: 10], i.e., mountains that are fixed, ﴿lest it shake with you﴾ [Luqman: 10], i.e., lest it sway and destroy you because of the agitation (al-jayashan) of strength within its interior. ﴿And He dispersed therein every kind of moving creature﴾ [Luqman: 10], i.e., every type of its kinds. ﴿And We sent down﴾ [Luqman: 10], i.e., for your preservation and the preservation of your animals, and for your benefit and the benefit of your animals, ﴿water from the sky and caused to grow therein every noble kind﴾ [Luqman: 10], i.e., a class of foods and medicines, ﴿noble﴾ [Luqman: 10], i.e., abundant in benefits.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 31, verses 11–12:

The discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He:

[11–12] ﴿This is the creation of Allah. So show me what those besides Him have created. Rather, the wrongdoers are in manifest error.﴾ ﴿And We certainly gave Luqman wisdom, [saying], "Be grateful to Allah. And whoever is grateful is only grateful for [the benefit of] himself. ﴿This﴾ means: what has been mentioned of the heavens and the earth and the related matters counted therein. ﴿is the creation of Allah﴾ means: His creation. ﴿So show me what those besides Him have created﴾ means: what you have taken as partners to Him, glorified is He, in worship. ﴿Rather, the wrongdoers are in manifest error﴾ is a transition (idrab, a shift from one point to another) away from rebuking them with what was mentioned, to recording upon them clear error. This calls for turning away from addressing them with the sound rational premises, because it is impossible for them to understand anything from them so as to be guided by it to knowledge of the falsehood of what they hold, or to be affected by the argument and rebuke so that they desist from it. The placing of the apparent noun in the place of their pronoun is to indicate that by their association (of partners with Allah) they are placing a thing in other than its proper place, transgressing the limits, and wronging themselves by exposing themselves to the everlasting punishment. This is what Abu al-Su'ud stated.

Then He, exalted, indicated that the falsehood of association (shirk) is spoken on the tongue of people of wisdom. How could it not be, when monotheism (tawhid) is the foundation of wisdom? This is in His words, glorified is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Luqman wisdom﴾ [Luqman: 12], meaning the perfection of the soul through theoretical sciences and a disposition for virtuous actions to the extent of human capacity, commanding him (to do so) through the tongue of a prophet or by way of inspiration (ilham); (according to the view of the majority, that he was a wise man). Whoever is given them has indeed been given much good. This is what al-Mahayimi said. The more apparent view is that "an" (that) is explanatory (mufassirah), since giving wisdom is in the sense of saying. Gratitude (shukr) is a word that encompasses all that the happiness of this world and the Hereafter revolves around, because the servant directs all that Allah has bestowed upon him towards that for which he was created. ﴿And whoever is grateful is only grateful for [the benefit of] himself﴾ [Luqman: 12], because the fruits of his gratitude return to him. ﴿And whoever is ungrateful - indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ [Luqman: 12], meaning: He is free of need of everything, so He does not need gratitude, and He is worthy of praise. Rather, every existing thing speaks His praise.

A note:

Ibn Kathir said: The early scholars (al-salaf) differed about Luqman: was he a prophet, or a righteous servant without prophethood, according to two views? The majority hold the second. It is said that he was a judge over the Children of Israel in the time of Dawud, peace be upon him. What has been narrated that he was a slave who had been subjected to servitude contradicts his being a prophet, because the messengers were sent among the noble lineages of their peoples. For this reason, the majority of the early scholars held that he was not a prophet. The claim that he was a prophet is only transmitted from Ikrimah, if the chain of narration to him is sound; for Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Waki' from Isra'il from Jabir from Ikrimah, who said: "Luqman was a prophet." Some have claimed that Luqman is Bal'am, mentioned in the Torah, who was a sage of an idolatrous people and was informed by Allah, exalted is He. He also went to an extreme in this comparison, claiming that the Arabic verb (laqama) means in Hebrew "balaa" (to swallow). And Allah knows best.

Al-Suyuti has versified those about whose prophethood there is disagreement, saying:

"The transmitters have differed concerning Khidr: it is said he is a prophet, or a saint, or a messenger.
Luqman, Dhu al-Qarnayn, Hawwa, Maryam... and suspension of judgment regarding all of them is the view of the one who venerates (the matter)."

Then Luqman, in his counsel to him to worship Allah alone, joined with it kindness to the two parents, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment﴾ [al-Isra': 23]. Allah, exalted is He, often joins these two together in the Noble Qur'an. And He said here...

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[13–14] ﴿And when Luqman said to his son, while he was admonishing him, "O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. ﴿And when Luqman said to his son, while he was admonishing him, "O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is a great wrong."﴾ ﴿And We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents﴾ [Luqman: 14]. These five are the foundation of gratitude and the structure built upon it. If any one of them is lacking, one of the foundations of gratitude is compromised. Whoever speaks about gratitude, his speech returns to these and revolves around them. End of quotation.

"Your mother, then your mother, then your mother," and then he said, "then your father." It is also reported of one of the Arabs that he carried his mother on his back to the pilgrimage, while he himself chanted:

I carry my mother, and she is the carrier,
she nurses me with milk and tender food.

And no parent is repaid for what he has done (for his child).

Second: The Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Kathīr said: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿and his weaning is within two years﴾ [Luqman: 14], is like His saying: ﴿And mothers nurse their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233]. [15] The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. And accompany them in this world with kindness. And follow the way of one who turns to Me in repentance. Then to Me will be your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do.﴾

﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾ That is: in associating with Me something you do not know to deserve worship, by blindly following them (taqlid). Al-Zamakhshari said: "By negating knowledge of it, He intends to negate it, meaning: do not associate with Me that which is not a thing, referring to the idols," like His words: ﴿what they call upon besides Him is nothing﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 42].

In al-Kashf, he said: "This is not of the kind of negating knowledge in order to negate existence, as was mentioned in al-Qasas. Otherwise He would have said 'that which does not exist.' Rather, He intends that its negation has been emphasized to the point that it is made as nothing, and then the emphasis was carried to the absolutely unknown."

Al-Shihab said: "This is a fine formulation, containing great emphasis."

﴿And accompany them in this world with kindness﴾ That is: good companionship that the Sharia approves and generosity requires.

Al-Suyuti said in al-Iklil: "The verse indicates that a parent is not to be obeyed in disbelief, yet is to be accompanied with kindness."

Then He explains the remainder of Luqman's counsels, by His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[16–17] ﴿O my son, indeed it, if it be the weight of a mustard seed and should be within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted.﴾ ﴿O my son, establish prayer and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination.﴾ [Luqman: 17]

﴿O my son, indeed it, if it be the weight of a mustard seed﴾ means: indeed the deed, whether of wrongdoing or of good, if it is, in its smallness, like a mustard seed: ﴿and it be within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth﴾, meaning: even though it is at the utmost limit of smallness, in the most hidden and most secure place, like the hollow of a rock, or wherever it may be in the upper or lower knowledge: ﴿Allah will bring it forth﴾, meaning: He will produce it and call to account for it: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle﴾, meaning: His knowledge and power penetrate everything: ﴿and Acquainted﴾, meaning: He knows the reality of things, so nothing is difficult for Him. This verse is like His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything﴾ [al-Anbiya: 47], and His words: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7] ﴿and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 8].

A subtle point:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿within a rock﴾, etc., are of the rhetorical device called al-tatmim (completion), for He completed its obscurity in itself with the obscurity of its place within the rock, and this is of the same kind as the saying of the poet:

"As if it were a banner-flag with fire upon its head."

﴿O my son, establish prayer﴾ [Luqman: 17], meaning: with its limits, obligations and times, to perfect yourself through the worship of your Lord: ﴿and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾ [Luqman: 17], to perfect others: ﴿and be patient over what befalls you﴾ [Luqman: 17], meaning: of trials and afflictions, or in what you have been commanded of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, because the one who calls to the truth is exposed to having harm inflicted upon him; and this is the more apparent. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted.﴾ ﴿O my son, establish prayer and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination.﴾ [Luqman: 17]

﴿O my son, indeed it, if it be the weight of a mustard seed﴾ means: indeed the deed, whether of wrongdoing or of good, if it is, in its smallness, like a mustard seed: ﴿and it be within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth﴾, meaning: even though it is at the utmost limit of smallness, in the most hidden and most secure place, like the hollow of a rock, or wherever it may be in the upper or lower knowledge: ﴿Allah will bring it forth﴾, meaning: He will produce it and call to account for it: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle﴾, meaning: His knowledge and power penetrate everything: ﴿and Acquainted﴾, meaning: He knows the reality of things, so nothing is difficult for Him. This verse is like His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything﴾ [al-Anbiya: 47], and His words: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7] ﴿and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 8].

A subtle point:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿within a rock﴾, etc., are of the rhetorical device called al-tatmim (completion), for He completed its obscurity in itself with the obscurity of its place within the rock, and this is of the same kind as the saying of the poet:

"As if it were a banner-flag with fire upon its head."

﴿O my son, establish prayer﴾ [Luqman: 17], meaning: with its limits, obligations and times, to perfect yourself through the worship of your Lord: ﴿and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾ [Luqman: 17], to perfect others: ﴿and be patient over what befalls you﴾ [Luqman: 17], meaning: of trials and afflictions, or in what you have been commanded of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, because the one who calls to the truth is exposed to having harm inflicted upon him; and this is the more apparent. It is matched by the verse: ﴿and they enjoined one another to the truth and enjoined one another to patience﴾ [al-Asr: 3]. ﴿Indeed, that﴾ [Luqman: 17] refers to patience, or to everything he was commanded: ﴿is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [Luqman: 17], meaning: of the matters that Allah has determined, that is, decreed with a decree of obligation.

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[18–19] ﴿And do not turn your cheek away from people in arrogance, and do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, Allah does not love everyone self-deluded and boastful.﴾ (p-4802) ﴿And be moderate in your walking, and lower your voice. Indeed, the most disagreeable of voices is the voice of donkeys.﴾ [Luqman: 19]

﴿And do not turn your cheek away from people﴾: that is, do not turn your face away from them when you speak to them or they speak to you, out of contempt for them and arrogance toward them. Rather, lower your side (to them) and open your face toward them, as came in the hadith: "Even if you meet your brother with a cheerful face." ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly﴾: that is, with vanity, being haughty. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love everyone self-deluded﴾: that is, one who is conceited in himself. ﴿boastful﴾: that is, over others. ﴿And be moderate in your walking﴾ [Luqman: 19]: that is, find a middle course between plodding and hurrying. ﴿And lower your voice﴾ [Luqman: 19]: that is, reduce its raising and restrain it, for it is made ugly by loudness, so that people reject it just as they reject the voice of donkeys. (Wahsh, "repugnance") is originally the opposite of intimacy and familiarity. So it is either a metaphor (majaz) or a metonymy (kinayah).

Al-Zamakhshari said: The donkey is a figure of speech for stern blame and vile insult, and so is its braying. Among their revulsion at mentioning it by itself, and their avoidance of its name, is that they refer to it by euphemism and avoid stating it explicitly; so they say "the long-eared one," just as unclean things are referred to by euphemism. It has been counted among the faults of etiquette that the mention of the donkey should occur in the gathering of people of honour (muruwwah). Some Arabs refuse to ride a donkey out of disdain, even if the journey demands it. Thus, comparing those who raise their voices to donkeys, and depicting their voices as braying, then omitting the word of comparison from the speech and presenting it in the form of a metaphor (isti'arah), and making them donkeys and their voice braying, is an extremely intense exaggeration (mubalaghah) (p-4803) in censure and disparagement, and an excessive discouragement from raising the voice and a warning against it, and an alert that it is in a place of Allah's displeasure. End of quote.

Note:

If they discourse on the remembrance of Allah, then send your arrow among them (join in). If they discourse on other than that, then turn away from them to others. The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 31, verses 20–21:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted:

[20–21] ﴿Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and has completed upon you His favors, outward and inward? Yet among the people is he who disputes concerning Allah without knowledge or guidance or an illuminating Book.﴾ (p-4804) ﴿And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has sent down," they say, "Rather, we will follow that upon which we found our fathers." Even if Satan was inviting them to the punishment of the Blaze?﴾ [Luqman: 21]

﴿Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, that is: of the stars, the sun, and the moon, from whose light they benefit, and what they produce in animals, plants, and inanimate things by His power, the Exalted. Likewise [He subjected] the rains, the clouds, and the heavenly phenomena which He created for the benefit of those to whom they are subjected. Likewise [He subjected] what He brought into being on the earth of settled places, trees, rivers, crops, and fruits, so that those to whom they are subjected may use them for what sustains their life, comfort, and happiness. ﴿And has completed upon you His favors, outward and inward﴾, that is: the sensible and the intelligible, such as the sending of messengers, the revelation of books, and the removal of doubts and defects. ﴿And among the people﴾, meaning those who deny His favor, the Exalted: ﴿is he who disputes concerning Allah﴾, that is: concerning His oneness and His sending of messengers: ﴿without knowledge﴾, that is: without a decisive proof derived from reason; ﴿or guidance﴾, that is: a transmitted evidence from a Prophet; ﴿or an illuminating Book﴾, that is: one sent down from Him, the Exalted, but [he relies] merely on imitation. And "illuminating" means: one that rescues from the darkness of ignorance and misguidance.

﴿And when it is said to them﴾ [Luqman: 21], that is: to those who dispute, and the plural is used in view of meaning: ﴿"Follow what Allah has sent down," they say, "Rather, we will follow that upon which we found our fathers." Even if Satan was inviting them to the punishment of the Blaze?﴾ [Luqman: 21], that is: he was inviting their fathers to beliefs and deeds which are the causes of punishment, as if he were inviting them to the very punishment itself. So they are heading toward it according to his call, and whoever is like this, how can he be followed?

Ibn Zayd said: it is one who is intermediate in action. [30–32] ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Great.﴾ ﴿Do you not see that the ships sail through the sea by the favour of Allah, that He may show you of His signs? Surely in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful person.﴾ [Luqman: 31] ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them safely to the land, some of them are moderate. And none rejects Our signs except every treacherous, ungrateful one.﴾ [Luqman: 32]

﴿That﴾ refers to what has been mentioned of the breadth of knowledge, the comprehensiveness of power, the wonders of creation, and the exclusiveness of the Creator to them: ﴿because Allah is the Truth﴾, i.e., because of the fact that He is the Truth, His existence and His divinity. ﴿And what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and Allah is the Most High, the Great.﴾ ﴿Do you not see that the ships sail through the sea by the favour of Allah﴾ [Luqman: 31], i.e., by His kindness in providing its causes. ﴿That He may show you of His signs. Surely in that are signs for every ṣabbār﴾ [Luqman: 31], i.e., one of great patience in adversity and hardship; ﴿shakūr﴾ [Luqman: 31], i.e., one of abundant gratitude for blessings, by fulfilling their due.

﴿And when He covers them﴾ [Luqman: 32], i.e., overtakes them and surrounds them; ﴿a wave like shadows﴾ [Luqman: 32], i.e., like clouds and veils; ﴿they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Luqman: 32], i.e., they turn to Him, the Exalted, alone, with the removal of what contends with the innate nature (fiṭrah) of desire and imitation, because of the harm that has befallen them.

﴿But when He delivers them safely to the land, some of them are moderate (muqtaṣid)﴾ [Luqman: 32]. Ibn Kathir said: Mujahid said: i.e., a disbeliever. It seems he interpreted "muqtaṣid" here as "the denier," as the Exalted said: ﴿But when He delivers them safely to the land, behold, they associate partners﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 65]. Ibn Zayd said: it is one who is intermediate in action. And this which Ibn Zayd said is what is meant in the Exalted's words: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate﴾ [Fatir: 32], so the muqtaṣid here is the one intermediate in action. It is possible that it is also meant here, and it is a form of rebuke against one who witnessed those great terrors and matters, and the dazzling signs at sea, and then, after Allah had bestowed upon him deliverance, he should have answered that with complete action and diligent worship, and hastening to good deeds; so whoever is moderate after that is, in this state, negligent. And Allah knows best. End of quotation.

﴿And none rejects Our signs except every khattār﴾ [Luqman: 32], i.e., treacherous, breaker of the innate covenant and of the firm resolve made at the time of the sea's terror; ﴿kafūr﴾ [Luqman: 32], i.e., excessive in denying His blessings, not fulfilling their rights, nor employing them in what He loves.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 31, verse 33:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[33] ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord and dread a Day when no father will avail his son at all, nor will a son avail his father at all. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, so let not the worldly life delude you, and let not the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah.﴾

﴿O mankind, fear your Lord and dread a Day when no father will avail his son at all, nor will a son avail his father at all﴾ That is: neither of them will suffice the other in anything, due to the severing of ties on that terrible Day (p-4808). Abu al-Su'ud said: The change of wording in the second clause serves to indicate that the child is even more unlikely to be recompensed, and it cuts off the hope of those believers who might expect that they could benefit their unbelieving father in the Hereafter. ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾ That is, concerning reward and punishment; it is impossible that it be broken. ﴿So let not the worldly life delude you, and let not the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah﴾ That is: Satan.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[34] ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.﴾

﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour﴾, i.e., knowledge of the time of its establishment. ﴿And He sends down the rain﴾, i.e., at the time He has decreed and to the place He has specified in His knowledge. ﴿And He knows what is in the wombs﴾, i.e., whether it is male or female, happy or wretched. ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾, i.e., of good or evil. ﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die﴾, i.e., in its own land or elsewhere, because Allah, exalted is He, alone possesses the knowledge of that. It has been reported that these five are called "the keys of the unseen" (mafatih al-ghayb). ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted﴾, i.e., with what has been and what will be, and with the outward and inward aspects of things. There is no god but Him.
